notes.meaning: Paul reminds believers of what they were like before God saved them. Without spiritual life, people are like corpses, entirely cut off from God and unable to reach Him on their own. Our wrong choices and sinful acts proved that we were spiritually dead.

In that dead condition, people follow the broken ways and customs of this world. They are guided by Satan, described as the ruler over unseen evil spirits, who actively works inside people who disobey God. Sinners live as captives under his dark power without even knowing it.

All people, whether Jews or Gentiles, once lived this way, driven by bodily cravings and sinful thoughts. Because of our fallen human nature, we were all born deserving God's holy anger against sin. In ourselves, no one was better than anyone else or had any claim on God.

God did not leave humanity to perish in that hopeless state. Out of His endless mercy and deep love, He showed compassion to us even when we were entirely unlovely. His great love is the only reason and starting place for our rescue.

Even while we were completely dead in our sins, God gave us new spiritual life together with Christ. Salvation—being rescued from sin and judgment—comes entirely by grace, which is God's free and undeserved favor. We did not earn this life; God gave it to us by joining us to Jesus when He rose.

God did not stop at giving us life; He also raised us up with Christ and seated us with Him in heaven. Because believers are spiritually united to Jesus as their Head, their place of honor and safety in heaven is already guaranteed. We can live above the pull of this world because our true home is with Him.

God did all this so that throughout every coming age and into eternity, He could put the boundless wealth of His grace on display. The Church stands as a lasting monument to show the universe how kind and patient God is through Christ Jesus. Future generations can look at what He did for sinners and find encouragement to seek His mercy.

God saves us purely by His grace through faith, which means trusting Jesus rather than our own efforts. This deliverance is entirely God's free gift, not something we produced or earned by living a good life. Because no human effort brought it about, no one can brag or take credit for being saved.

differ.view: Teaches that God's electing grace is sovereignly given only to the elect, cannot be resisted, and grants the gift of faith apart from human free will.
Teaches that God's grace is offered to all people, restoring human free will so that anyone can freely choose or refuse to believe.
Teaches that salvation and faith are entirely God's work given through the Word and sacraments, without any human cooperation or decision.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Understands this passage to refer to initial justification, which is received by grace through faith apart from prior works, while works done in grace remain necessary in the ongoing process of salvation.

notes.meaning: Believers are God's own new creation, crafted by His hand in Christ Jesus like a work of art. We are not saved by good works, but we are saved for the purpose of doing them. Long ago, God prepared helpful tasks and holy paths for us to walk in every day.

Gentile believers are told to remember how bleak life was before they came to know Christ. They were looked down upon by the Jewish people as outsiders who had no share in Israel's nation or God's sacred promises. In that state, they wandered through the world without any true hope and without the living God.

Everything changed when these outsiders were united to Christ Jesus. Those who were once far away from God and His people have now been brought close. This close relationship was purchased entirely by the sacrificial blood of Christ on the cross.

Christ Himself is the peace between divided peoples and between sinners and God. By dying on the cross, He set aside the Jewish ceremonial laws that had acted like a dividing wall between Jews and Gentiles. Out of these two separated groups, He created a single new spiritual family in one body, completely putting to death the hostility through His sacrifice.

Jesus announced the good news of peace both to Gentiles who were far off and to Jews who were near. Through Him alone, both groups now have direct entrance into the presence of the Father. This shared approach to God is guided and empowered by the one Holy Spirit.

Gentile believers are no longer treated as foreigners or temporary guests who lack full rights. Instead, they are full citizens of God's holy kingdom alongside all His people. Even more closely, they are now beloved members of God's own family and household.

This spiritual family is like a grand building resting on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, whose teachings reveal God's truth. Jesus Christ Himself is the chief cornerstone, the essential foundation block that sets the lines and holds the whole structure together. Everything in the church must align with Him.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Teaches that while all the apostles serve as foundation stones under Christ the chief cornerstone, Peter holds a unique role of leadership among them as the rock.

notes.meaning: Joined firmly to Christ, the whole building of believers fits together smoothly and grows like a living temple dedicated to the Lord. Every Christian is being built into this structure alongside others. Together, the church becomes the spiritual home where God Himself lives by His Holy Spirit.
